content.text:
Fixed. The change is in the working tree (uncommitted) and ready to be committed/pushed.

## Root cause

In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, the "Sign container image with Cosign" step runs `cosign sign` interactively. In GitHub Actions there's no TTY, so when cosign prompts:

```
Are you sure you would like to continue? [y/N]
```

it can't get an answer and fails with `user declined the prompt` (exit code 1).

Note: the "tag, not a digest" message is only a warning — it wasn't the cause of the failure.

## Fix

Added the `--yes` flag to `cosign sign`, which skips the interactive confirmation (appropriate for CI):

```yaml
      - name: Sign container image with Cosign
        env:
          COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL: 1
        run: |
          cosign sign ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }} \
            --oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
            --oidc-client-id ${{ github.repository_owner }} \
            --yes
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
```

YAML validates OK. The `--yes` flag is supported by the installed `sigstore/cosign-installer@v3.8.1`.

Would you like me to commit and push this change to `main` so the next release run picks it up?

Not certain this is the ideal fix.

The warning
> WARNING: Image reference ghcr.io/albuskavaliro/autoapprover/auto-approver-worker:main uses a tag, not a digest, to identify the image to sign.

and the rest clearly says this option will be removed in the future. Shouldn't we try to cosign the image with it's SHA256 instead? As suggested?

You're right — signing by tag is the deeper problem, and `--yes` alone just papers over it while the deprecation warning remains. Let me switch the sign step to sign by the image's SHA256 digest instead.

The build step (`docker/build-push-action`, `id: build`) exposes the pushed image's digest as `steps.build.outputs.digest`, so I'll reference that.

            --oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
            --oidc-client-id ${{ github.repository_owner }} \
            --yes
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}

content.text:
The fix is in place and YAML validates. Here's what changed and why:

**Why sign by digest:** The warning explicitly says tags will be removed as a way to identify images to sign, and signing by tag can result in signing a different image than intended. `docker/build-push-action` (used with `id: build`) exposes the pushed image's digest via `steps.build.outputs.digest`, so the sign step now targets:

```
ghcr.io/albuskavaliro/autoapprover/auto-approver-worker@sha256:...
```

instead of `...:main`.

**Why `--yes` is still needed:** Even when signing by digest, keyless/OIDC signing prompts:

```
Are you sure you would like to continue? [y/N]
```

(the Sigstore hosted-service terms). CI has no TTY to answer it, so `--yes` skips that interactive confirmation — appropriate for an automated pipeline.

The sign step only runs on non-PR events, so `push` is `true` there and `steps.build.outputs.digest` will be populated.

The change is uncommitted in the working tree. Would you like me to commit and push it to `main`?
